method: Built-in image_gen; model revision/seed/usage price not exposed
scope: Four named source-art gaps; all outputs are unaccepted source candidates. No per-frame generation and no costume character builders.

shared_view.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: one editable 2D cutout rig source sheet, landscape 1536x1024 if possible, true transparent RGBA. Image 1 is the APPROVED Roshan identity, palette, painted outlines and original outfit. Image 2 supplies the approved right-facing swimming view only; do not copy its arm-paddling action or its low resolution. Create the named missing shared swimming-view PARTS, never a new costume character or a set of complete characters. Keep this exact little mermaid child: round brown eyes, warm brown bob curls, one tied rainbow ponytail, pink short-sleeved bodice, violet/aqua sparkling tail and a single rainbow two-lobed fin. Polished painted 2D storybook, crisp anti-aliased dark contours, matching the references. No relighting or redesign. Neutral gently extended horizontal swimming posture, looking toward the RIGHT in three-quarter view, tail extends LEFT; keep head/body proportions like the approved source. The core body should have room to flex, not the tightly curled J tail. Deliver ONE source sheet with separated NON-TOUCHING painted cutout pieces, fully visible and no text, boxes, labels, background or shadows. Upper row: (left) one head with brown bob curls, BOTH eyes visible in right-facing three-quarter view, tiny painted neck overlap and ponytail root/tie fixed at its back, no tiara baked into it; (middle) the one flowing rainbow ponytail free length, trailing LEFT with a short hidden brown/root overlap on its RIGHT attachment end; (right) two relaxed child arms with natural hands, complete shoulder-to-fingertips, drawn separately in the matching swimming perspective. Lower row: (left) torso wearing her original opaque pink bodice, chest/neck opening toward RIGHT and waist opening toward LEFT, with round painted overlap extensions at its endpoints; (middle) one smoothly tapered long gently curved violet/aqua sparkling tail shaft WITHOUT the fin, thick waist end on RIGHT and narrow fin attachment on LEFT; (right) three matching ONE-fin state cutouts vertically spaced: relaxed broad rainbow two-lobed fin, feathered narrow edge-view of that SAME fin, broad cupped braking view of that SAME fin. Each fin attaches at its RIGHT tip and extends LEFT; preserve rainbow band order, one fin with two lobes, no extra fins or ribbons. The two lobe silhouettes must match her fin design; edge and brake states reveal plausible painted surfaces, not a squashed copy. Leave enough real transparent gap to isolate every part. Keep the same scale between corresponding fin states and among the body parts; head roughly 220px tall and tail shaft roughly 450px long at requested sheet size. Paint real hidden overlap pixels at shoulders, neck, waist, hair root and fin root so joints can close, while preserving the authored contour. IMPORTANT: this is a source parts kit for ONE shared skeleton, not multiple complete Roshan drawings. No nudity, no exposed chest, no whole-figure costume variants, no anatomy diagrams, no detached extra fingers, no writing or generator coordinate marks.

ballet.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: ONE garment-only Ballet skin source sheet for an existing shared 2D mermaid rig, true transparent RGBA, landscape 1536x1024. Image1 is the shared rig PART SHAPES and painting style, NOT a character to redraw. Image2 is the existing Fashion Designer Ballet dress, Image3 its tail cover, Image4 its bow/pearl headpiece. Preserve those costume designs: pink and peach satin, cream bows, gold scalloped piping, pearls and shell-shaped bodice. Produce ONLY separated clothes, no character, no face, hair, skin, hands, anatomy or rainbow fins. Paint the missing three-quarter-view garment pieces to fit the same torso and curved tail-shaft shapes in Image1. Left third of sheet: compact upright three-quarter bodice, round neckline and shoulder openings like the pink shirt in Image1, pearl waist bow and a short scalloped peach skirt; preserve silhouette space for the real arms and neck, no black fill in openings. Bottom middle: a LONG gently curved tail-cover sleeve matching Image1 tail shaft: thick open waist at upper RIGHT, smooth S-curve tapering toward lower LEFT, narrow open peduncle end at LEFT; use the same approximate length/width and endpoint direction as that source tail. Adapt the existing pink/peach overlapping panels, pearl chains and gold piping along this curve without adding a fin or extending it into a full character. Top middle: two separate small matching shoulder puff/strap pieces. Top right: the existing pink bow and pearl shell headpiece, fitted to a right-facing three-quarter head, as a detached wearable accessory. Five separate islands only, generous transparent gaps, no text, outlines around cells, glow or background. Keep real antialiasing, painted texture, crisp dark contours and coherent perspective. Same relative source scale as Image1. This sheet becomes garment attachments on the ONE shared skeleton; do not render a complete costumed Roshan.

Crisp antialiased dark contours and polished 2D storybook paint like the approved inputs. Real transparent gaps and clear shoulder/neck/waist openings. This is garment art/data for ONE shared actor; it must not become a new costumed character.

neck.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Named missing shared rig joint surface: ONE small painted neck-and-shoulder YOKE cutout for the exact child mermaid Roshan shown in the reference parts sheet. True transparent RGBA, square image. This is a technical overlap insert used beneath her existing fully opaque dress, NOT an undressed character. Draw only the visible neck, collarbone/collar area and two small shoulder attachment ends; stop well above the chest garment, no head/face, breasts, torso, arms or complete person. Match the reference's warm light-peach skin color, polished 2D storybook shading and crisp dark outline. It must join an upright right-facing three-quarter head at its TOP-RIGHT and a diagonally swimming torso extending toward BOTTOM-LEFT: the neck rises upright at the right, with gently sloping shoulders spreading leftward/downward into the collar area. Show a natural connected neck/shoulder silhouette, not a straight tilted plate. Leave generous painted hidden overlap beneath the dress neckline and behind the head/upper-arm pieces, with a smooth plain lower edge that will be hidden. No clothing, accessories, props, background, shadows outside the piece, glow, labels or text. Use the actual reference's 2D perspective and palette, do not redesign anatomy. This single shared neck/shoulder insert will remain exactly unchanged when different costumes are swapped.
